rounds.text: While low valuation multiples might draw attention, Nahar Polyfilms suffers from medium-term top-line stagnation with a 3-year compounded sales growth rate of -1% [E16], trailing well behind the sector median sales growth of 14.9% [E69]. This lack of revenue expansion is accompanied by decelerating earnings growth [E65]. The company has also demonstrated persistently weak capital efficiency, highlighted by a low 3-year return on equity of 6.19% [E59] and a 3-year median return on equity of just 6% [E28]. Over longer horizons, return metrics remain muted, with 5-year and 10-year median returns on equity standing at 8% [E27] and 9% [E26], respectively. Conceded: the business has shown recent fundamental momentum, with year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% [E63], a recent ROE reaching 13.3% [E13], and a 5-year compounded sales growth rate of 18% [E15]. Nonetheless, the broader track record of negative 3-year sales growth [E16] and sub-10% historical median ROE figures [E26, E27, E28] indicates that recent performance may not translate into reliable long-term compounding.
